subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Journalist Jon Krakauer's book Into Thin Air is about the 1996 Everest disaster.
• The 1996 Everest disaster was a tragic event in mountaineering history when eight climbers died during summit attempts on Mount Everest.
• To document this event, Krakauer narrates his own firsthand experience as a member of one of the expeditions, including those led by Rob Hall and Scott Fischer.
• The book won the American Library Association's Alex Award in 1998.
• It was also a finalist for the Pulitzer Prize in General Nonfiction.
prompt: Which choice most effectively uses information from the notes to emphasize how Krakauer documents the 1996 Everest disaster?

choices.A: The 1996 Everest disaster was one of the deadliest seasons in the mountain's history, with eight climbers losing their lives.
choices.B: Jon Krakauer chronicles the tragic events of the 1996 Everest disaster in gripping, firsthand detail by narrating his own experience as a member of one of the ill-fated expeditions, such as those led by Rob Hall and Scott Fischer.
choices.C: In 1997, Jon Krakauer's book Into Thin Air won not only the American Library Association's Alex Award but also became a finalist for the Pulitzer Prize.
choices.D: The fatal expedition led by Rob Hall is featured in the award-winning book Into Thin Air.

explanation: Choice B is the best answer because it directly emphasizes Krakauer's methodology for documenting the disaster. The phrase 'by narrating his own experience as a member of one of the ill-fated expeditions' explicitly addresses how he documents the event—through firsthand, personal narration. This choice captures the key information from the notes about his approach and mentions specific expedition leaders, making it most effective for the stated goal.
